places.name: Udupi Sri Krishna Temple
places.significance: The historic Krishna temple at the heart of Udupi, associated with Madhwacharya and the Ashta Mathas, and famous for the deity being viewed through the Kanakana Kindi.
places.moreinfo: Tourists can explore Udupi's spiritual heritage and temple traditions.

places.name: Anantheshwara Temple
places.significance: One of the oldest temples in Udupi, traditionally associated with Lord Shiva and the early spiritual life of Madhwacharya.
places.moreinfo: Tourists can learn about Udupi's early spiritual and temple history.

places.name: Chandramouleshwara Temple
places.significance: An ancient Shiva temple opposite Anantheshwara, associated with the traditional legend of Chandra, the Moon god.
places.moreinfo: Tourists can visit a historic shrine and explore local religious traditions.

places.name: Bannanje Mahalingeshwara Temple
places.significance: An ancient stone temple in Bannanje traditionally associated with the 8th-9th centuries and with the religious history of the Udupi region.
places.moreinfo: Tourists can observe traditional stone architecture and regional religious history.

places.name: Ambalpadi Janardhana and Mahakali Temple
places.significance: A historic temple complex featuring Lord Janardhana and Goddess Mahakali, with a traditional sacred pond and long-standing cultural importance in Udupi.
places.moreinfo: Tourists can experience a living temple complex and its cultural traditions.

places.name: Mount Rosary Church
places.significance: A historic Roman Catholic church in Kallianpur near Udupi, built in 1837 and known for its coastal Christian heritage and stained-glass interiors.
places.moreinfo: Tourists can study the church's architecture and coastal Christian history.

places.name: Our Lady of Miracles Cathedral, Kallianpur
places.significance: A historic Catholic cathedral at Kallianpur representing the long-standing Indo-Portuguese and Christian heritage of coastal Udupi.
places.moreinfo: Tourists can explore the region's diverse religious and architectural heritage.

places.name: Barkur Heritage Town
places.significance: An ancient settlement on the banks of the Sita River that was an important regional centre under the Alupas and later dynasties, known for its concentration of historic temples and ruins.
places.moreinfo: Tourists can explore historic ruins and the political history of coastal Karnataka.

places.name: Kathale Basadi, Barkur
places.significance: An ancient Jain monument at Barkur built from dark stone, featuring ruined mandapas and a prominent monolithic victory pillar.
places.moreinfo: Tourists can examine Jain architecture and the remains of Barkur's historic landscape.

places.name: Panchalingeshwara Temple, Barkur
places.significance: One of Barkur's major historic temples, dedicated to five manifestations of Shiva and noted for its traditional coastal temple architecture.
places.moreinfo: Tourists can learn about temple design and Shaiva traditions in Barkur.

places.name: Batte Vinayaka Temple, Barkur
places.significance: An old Barkur shrine dedicated to Ganesha, known for its historic stone image and its place within the ancient temple landscape of Barkur.
places.moreinfo: Tourists can visit a historic shrine within the wider heritage town of Barkur.

places.name: Barkur Fort Ruins
places.significance: The remains of a historic fortification at Barkur, reflecting the town's importance as a strategic and political centre in coastal Karnataka.
places.moreinfo: Tourists can investigate the remains and Barkur's role in regional history.

places.name: Suralu Palace
places.significance: A rare surviving mud-and-timber palace associated with the Tolaha rulers, dating to around 1500 CE and combining Hindu and Jain decorative traditions.
places.moreinfo: Tourists can study historic building materials and blended decorative traditions.

places.name: Mahalinga Temple, Brahmavara
places.significance: A historic Shiva temple in Brahmavara traditionally dated to around the 9th century and representative of early temple traditions in coastal Karnataka.
places.moreinfo: Tourists can explore early temple traditions in coastal Karnataka.

places.name: Varanga Jain Basadi
places.significance: A historic Jain temple complex at Varanga, famous for its tranquil setting and the basadi located beside and within the sacred lake landscape.
places.moreinfo: Tourists can experience Jain heritage in a distinctive lake setting.

places.name: Karkala Gomateshwara Statue
places.significance: A 42-foot monolithic statue of Bahubali erected in 1432, one of the most important Jain monuments in the Udupi region.
places.moreinfo: Tourists can study monumental sculpture and medieval Jain heritage.

places.name: Chaturmukha Basadi, Karkala
places.significance: A distinctive Jain basadi in Karkala with four symmetrical entrances, representing the region's important medieval Jain architectural tradition.
places.moreinfo: Tourists can examine the basadi's symmetry and medieval Jain design.

places.name: St. Lawrence Shrine Basilica, Attur
places.significance: A historic Catholic shrine in Attur near Karkala, dating to the 18th century and known for its distinctive religious and architectural heritage.
places.moreinfo: Tourists can explore Attur's religious history and distinctive architecture.

places.name: Anegudde Sri Vinayaka Temple
places.significance: A historic Ganesha temple at Anegudde in the Kundapura region, situated on a hillock and traditionally counted among the important sacred sites of the region.
places.moreinfo: Tourists can experience a major pilgrimage site in the Kundapura region.

places.name: Kotilingeshwara Temple, Koteshwara
places.significance: An important historic Shiva temple at Koteshwara, associated with the ancient religious landscape of the Kundapura region.
places.moreinfo: Tourists can learn about the ancient religious landscape of Kundapura.

places.name: Basrur Heritage Village
places.significance: A historic settlement near Kundapura known for its old temples, inscriptions, merchant-guild history, and importance as an ancient port town.
places.moreinfo: Tourists can explore trade, inscriptions, and the history of coastal settlements.

places.name: Nakhareshwara Temple, Basrur
places.significance: An historically significant temple at Basrur associated with a medieval merchant guild and an inscription dating to the 12th century.
places.moreinfo: Tourists can connect religious heritage with medieval trade history.

places.name: Tuluveshwara Temple, Basrur
places.significance: An old Shiva temple in Basrur whose surviving shrine is surrounded by vegetation, forming part of the area's historic temple landscape.
places.moreinfo: Tourists can observe how historic shrines remain part of the local landscape.

places.name: Keshavanatheshwara Temple, Moodugallu
places.significance: A historic Shiva shrine at Moodugallu known for its traditional coastal architecture and nearby natural laterite rock caves.
places.moreinfo: Tourists can explore the relationship between temple architecture and the natural setting.

places.name: St. Mary's Island Geological Heritage Site
places.significance: A protected geological heritage destination off Malpe, famous for its distinctive hexagonal columnar basalt formations created by ancient volcanic activity.
places.moreinfo: Tourists can study coastal geology and distinctive volcanic rock formations.
